producthunt.author: danshipit
producthunt.body:
RankSpot: Pay-as-you-go SEO and AI Search execution layer for agents RankSpot is the SEO and AI Search execution layer for agents. Connect the MCP to Claude or ChatGPT in 2 minutes and your agent does the work: it writes articles from what already ranks on Google in 100+ languages, publishes them, and pitches ranking sites from your mailbox for backlinks. Run every client or business from one chat. No subscription: $3 an article, $0.004 a prompt check, reading your data free. Start with $1 of credit and a free article.

Hey Product Hunt 👋

Dan here, co-founder of RankSpot.

Last time we launched, RankSpot only generated content on autopilot. Since then we've onboarded 1,000+ customers, and their feedback shaped our improved product. So we set out to build something no other SEO tool could do, and focused on these things:

1️⃣ Execution → Most SEO tools stop at the data

Congrats on the launch! Does it support Shopify?

Running a small web agency, the "manage multiple clients from one chat" part is what caught my eye. Can spend caps and scheduled tasks be set per client, so one client's article budget never bleeds into another's? And on WordPress, do articles land as drafts by default? I'd want a human pass on tone before anything goes live under a client's name.

Templify AI: Powerful content editor for people who aren’t editors Templify is an all-in-one video, photo, and carousel editor for iPhone. With 1,200+ designer templates, it turns clips and photos into Reels, TikToks, YouTube Shorts, and collages in minutes, no timeline needed. producthunt.author: fmerian
producthunt.body:
beacon.sh: Open-source self-improving memory for AI coding agents Beacon turns agent sessions across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, and 20+ other harnesses into a compounding knowledge layer, so every agent starts smarter than the last. It captures every agent trace across your environment and turns activity into clear operational visibility. Get started for free at beacon.sh

One of my favorite things about Beacon is that it makes your coding agents smarter the more you use them.

For everyone in the Product Hunt community building and shipping with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or other coding agents, you've probably experienced how frustrating it is to solve the same problem multiple times across different sessions and tools!

<

Memory is where most agents fall apart for me, so this is the right problem to go after. The part id push on is source and staleness. A memory learned from a trace 3 weeks ago can be confidently wrong after a refactor, and then every agent sharing it inherits the mistake. Does each memory point back to the trace it came from, and does anything expire it when the code it refers to changes? We ma

Love the idea of carrying lessons across coding agents. How does Beacon handle it when two agents learn conflicting things about the same codebase?

producthunt.body:

AgentKit handles auth and integrations, so every action runs as the user who asked, within the scopes they granted. Give each agent only the tools its job needs with Virtual MCP Servers. Free tier: 10,000 tool calls a month.

producthunt.author: justin2025
producthunt.body:
Glasshand: Give your agent a real iPhone and Mac Glasshand gives your AI agents real iPhones and Macs to work on. Connect Claude Code, Codex, or any other agent, and it can rent a device with a single prompt. The hardware sits in our data center, and your agent uses it the way you would: posting on TikTok, booking an Uber, or building and testing iOS apps. Each device is yours alone for as long as you rent it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset it.

Hey everyone. I’m Trevor, creator of Glasshand.

We’re the team behind Solid, from MIT, Berkeley, and Waterloo. We’ve raised $6M to build toward one goal: agents with human-level autonomy.


Agents are already smart enough for most of what you’d ask them to do, but a simple task on a phone can still leave yours waiting for you to open an app and tap a few buttons.

So Congrats on the launch! I wonder if this could replace our hardware to test a macOS agent we deploy through Intune. A few questions: - Do we get admin rights, with sudo to install LaunchDaemons? - Can we enrol the Mac in our own MDM (Intune through Company Portal) and install custom configuration profiles? - Which macOS version is it on, and how stable is the public IP and gateway? This is a great idea. I’ve found it annoying when building to have to manually test holding, scrubbing, finger-related UI interactions for my app… would be awesome to have my agents be able to interact with my product like I or anyone else would, without having to push and deploy everything for a little update to see if my scrubbing mechanic is a little better. Great work 👌🔥

source_items.body:
Glasshand: Give your agent a real iPhone and Mac Glasshand gives your AI agents real iPhones and Macs to work on. Connect Claude Code, Codex, or any other agent, and it can rent a device with a single prompt. The hardware sits in our data center, and your agent uses it the way you would: posting on TikTok, booking an Uber, or building and testing iOS apps. Each device is yours alone for as long as you rent it. When you’re done, we erase your data and factory-reset it.

Hey everyone. I’m Trevor, creator of Glasshand.

We’re the team behind Solid, from MIT, Berkeley, and Waterloo. We’ve raised $6M to build toward one goal: agents with human-level autonomy.


Agents are already smart enough for most of what you’d ask them to do, but a simple task on a phone can still leave yours waiting for you to open an app and tap a few buttons.

So Congrats on the launch! I wonder if this could replace our hardware to test a macOS agent we deploy through Intune. A few questions: - Do we get admin rights, with sudo to install LaunchDaemons? - Can we enrol the Mac in our own MDM (Intune through Company Portal) and install custom configuration profiles? - Which macOS version is it on, and how stable is the public IP and gateway? This is a great idea. I’ve found it annoying when building to have to manually test holding, scrubbing, finger-related UI interactions for my app… would be awesome to have my agents be able to interact with my product like I or anyone else would, without having to push and deploy everything for a little update to see if my scrubbing mechanic is a little better. Great work 👌🔥
